definitions.explanation: Describes a building that has three above-ground floors. Formed from the counter 三階 (three floors) plus 建て (built, constructed), this is part of the productive ～階建て pattern used to describe the number of stories in any building.

examples.japanese: {三階建|さんがいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}んでいる→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
examples.english: I live in a three-story house.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{辺|あた}り→辺り：01770_atari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{三階建|さんがいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦アパート→アパート：01012_apaato⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: There are many three-story apartment buildings in this area.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{校舎|こうしゃ}→校舎：02801_kousha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{三階建|さんがいだ}て⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{屋上|おくじょう}→屋上：01341_okujou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦プール→プール：02958_puuru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{付|つ}いている→付く：01960_tsuku⟧。
examples.english: The new school building is three stories tall and has a pool on the roof.

notes:
Part of the productive ～⟦{階建|かいだ}て→階建て：29226_kaidate⟧ pattern used to describe the number of stories in a building. The pattern is: number + ⟦{階|かい}→階：01034_kai⟧ + {建|だ}て.

COMMON PATTERN EXAMPLES:
- ⟦{二階建|にかいだ}て→二階建て：03001_nikaidate⟧: two-story
- {三階建|さんがいだ}て: three-story
- ⟦{五階建|ごかいだ}て→五階建て：28474_gokaidate⟧: five-story
- {十階建|じゅっかいだ}て: ten-story

USAGE:
This compound functions as a noun that modifies other nouns with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧, or is used as a prenominal modifier with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ omitted. In real estate listings and architecture, this is one of the most basic building specifications. Note that ⟦{三階|さんがい}→三階：27617_sangai⟧ uses the reading がい (not かい) due to sequential voicing (rendaku) after さん.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{三階|さんがい}→三階：27617_sangai⟧: third floor — refers to a specific floor rather than the building's total number of stories
- ⟦{平屋|ひらや}→平屋：15682_hiraya⟧: single-story house — a specific architectural term rather than a numbered description
